# My plan for this year — Lao Wang, 59, Quzhou

Alright, let me think through this. I've been growing wheat and maize on this land for 40 years, same as my father before me. Same two crops, same rotation, same calendar. I don't read much — never went to school — but my hands know this soil.

**About the land and the family**

I've got 12 mu. Not a lot, but enough to feed us and put a bit aside if the weather cooperates. There's six of us at home on paper, but really it's me and my wife doing the farming now. My elder son works construction in Handan, comes back for wheat harvest if I call him. My younger boy's in the factory. The grandkids are too small to help. So most of the work falls on me and the old woman, and we're not as quick as we used to be.

**Wheat — my winter crop**

I plant around Cold Dew (寒露), sometime in the first or second week of October, after the maize comes off. Same as always. I buy seed from the township co-op — that Jimai variety that everyone uses, about 8 kg per mu sowed thick because the late planting needs it. I don't save seed anymore, the new stuff yields better.

For fertilizer, before plowing I put down one bag of compound 15-15-15 per mu — that's 50 kg. Then after Spring Festival, when the wheat comes out of dormancy and I see it greening up, I broadcast urea, about 20 kg per mu. That's how I've always done it. My neighbor Lao Liu said last year he tried less urea and his wheat still looked fine, but I'm not ready to change. Two hundred yuan of fertilizer is cheap if it means another 50 kg of wheat.

Irrigation — I pump three times usually. Winter watering before the ground freezes so the roots don't get hurt. Then at returning-green in early March. Then at jointing in April when the wheat is stretching up. The well is metered so every watering costs me — maybe 30 yuan a mu each time. If it rains good in April I might skip the jointing one to save money, but you can't skip the winter watering.

Herbicide once in March for the wild oat and broadleaves. One spray. If I see rust or powdery mildew I'll spray a fungicide but usually I don't bother unless it looks bad.

I hire a combine at harvest, around Mangzhong (芒种), first week of June. Pay by the mu. My son might come help but mostly the combine handles it now, and then I need to get the stubble chopped and the field ready for maize fast — only a few days between.

Last year I got about 420 kg per mu. Year before that 450. I'll plan for 400 to be safe.

**Maize — my summer crop**

Soon as the wheat is off, I direct-seed maize into the stubble with a hired planter — no plowing, no time for it. Mid-June. I buy hybrid seed every year, that Zhengdan series, about 50 yuan a mu for the seed. Can't save hybrid seed, no point trying.

For fertilizer on maize I use less than on wheat — maize is tougher, and by summer the rain usually does half the work for me. One bag of compound at planting, about 40 kg per mu, and then around the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口) in late July I topdress 15 kg of urea per mu when I'm hoeing anyway.

Irrigation — maize gets maybe one or two waterings. If we have a dry June I water right after planting to get the stand up. If July-August is dry at tasseling I water again. Good rainy summer and I might not water at all and save the pumping money.

Spray herbicide after planting for the weeds. Sometimes an insecticide for the borer if I see the eggs on the leaves, but I don't spray unless I need to.

Harvest late September, hire the combine again. Last few years I got around 450-480 kg per mu. Going to plan for 450.

**Money**

I figure total inputs will be somewhere around 10,500-11,000 yuan for the whole year across both crops. That's most of my cash on hand from last year's sales. If prices of fertilizer go up again I'll just put a little less, not change everything. My wife always says keep some money in the drawer for when someone gets sick.
